title: Fearlessness, the ninth Guru's gift
hookLine: not being scared, and not being scary: the ninth Guru holds both in one line

lines: BRAVE AND SHARP, OR GENTLE AND SILENT.
cards: Which is harder: not being scared, or not being scary? It's easy to practice one and forget the other. Some people get brave, and on the way they get loud, sharp, a little frightening to the people around them.
Others work so hard at being gentle that they never stand up to anything. The ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, puts both in one short verse near the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib.
Today, the gift Sikhs remember him for: fearlessness, with two halves.

teach.h: FRIGHTEN NO ONE, FEAR NO ONE.
teach.b: The verse is one of his saloks, paraphrased: one who frightens no one, and who fears no one else, listen, O my mind, says Nanak, call that one wise. The ninth Guru signs as Nanak, as the Gurus do in the Granth.
Frightening no one comes first. Fearlessness here isn't a warrior's swagger. It starts with the people around you being safe with you.
Now go back to the Mul Mantar, the root verse at the Granth's opening, and a word this path has met before.

teach.h: NIRBHAU AND NIRVAIR, SIDE BY SIDE.
teach.b: Among its words for the One are nirbhau and nirvair: without fear, and without enmity, side by side. The ninth Guru's salok takes those two qualities of God and sets them inside a human being.
Without fear, you don't bow to threats. Without enmity, you don't make threats. They hold each other up.
A lot of frightening comes from being frightened. The boss who shouts is sometimes afraid of looking weak. The kid who bullies is sometimes scared at home.
And fear can make us small enough to stand by while others are frightened. Cut one root, and the other weakens.

Sikh tradition remembers Guru Tegh Bahadur living this line to the end, standing firm under pressure, without hatred for those applying it. That story comes in a couple of days. For now, just the line.

how: The saloks of Guru Tegh Bahadur are read near the end of a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, and Sikhs quote this verse on fearing no one and frightening no one when they speak of his life.

o: being so strong that others fear you
fearing no one, and frightening no one
never feeling afraid of anything at all

games.q: the line and its roots: tap the pairs.
p: frightens no one, fears no one
the salok calls that one wise
the root verse at the start of the Granth

s: the salok praises being fearless, and stops there
it pairs fearing no one with frightening no one, and frightening no one comes first.
nirbhau and nirvair sit side by side in the Mul Mantar
without fear and without enmity: qualities of the One.
the ninth Guru's saloks sit near the start of the Granth
they sit near the very end.

games.q: you've finally found the courage to stand up to someone. the adrenaline is high. how do you speak?
o: loud and sharp, so they know you mean it.
steady and gentle, without frightening anyone.
you don't: better to stay quiet.
games.why: the ninth Guru's salok calls wise the one who fears no one and frightens no one. courage without menace.

practice: First, bring to mind one person who might be a little afraid of you, a child, someone who reports to you, a waiter, and on the breath out, soften toward them.
Then bring to mind one thing you've been afraid to say or do, and on the breath in, let your back straighten.
Go back and forth, soft toward them, steady toward it, and if you pray, rest in the One who is without fear and without enmity.

wordCard.voice: Fearlessness. In the ninth Guru's salok, the wise one frightens no one and fears no one, both halves together. Today's word.

orig.note: without fear; a word for the One in the Mul Mantar, set beside nirvair, without enmity.

carryVoice: Your line: neither fear nor frighten. Brave and gentle, both halves at once. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Salok Mahala 9, Ang 1427 (one who gives fear to no one and fears no one is called wise)
Guru Granth Sahib, Mul Mantar, Ang 1 (nirbhau, nirvair)
